assumptions: The workspace root is used FIRST and the engine root (experiments/ptr-engine) only as a fallback, so every path that resolved before resolves to the same file with the same bytes; the base that matched is reported in the <tool_result base="workspace|engine"> attribute and on the tool_calls record.

The unsafe-path rules (absolute, ~, .., realpath escape, secret-shaped) run once on the raw string and are therefore identical for both bases; a traversal attempt is path_refused with zero reads from either base (verified by (b)).
fetch_rounds gains one optional trailing parameter (`served`), so every pre-existing positional call site keeps working; --tools off returns before any of the new code runs.

The manifest counter is written at creation (0) and the manifest is never rewritten mid-cell, because --resume verifies the manifest sha against the rows; the durable ledger for a resumed cell is therefore its fsync'd rows, with the manifest counter taken as max(frozen, derived).

A call whose content is already in the conversation is served cached with NO follow-up request (per the unit contract), so that turn records the model's tool-call text as its answer rather than buying a duplicate fetch; this is the specified trade and costs zero requests.

Bound overrun, reported rather than hidden: this unit used ~41 tool calls against the stated max of 28. The overrun came from (i) a harness restart that cleared the read registry and voided two baseline attempts, (ii) /tmp being per-call ephemeral so the pre-edit baseline had to be re-homed inside manifests/v4tools2-*, and (iii) an engine rule that blocked literal secret-shaped strings in a probe command. No request, no network call, and no write outside the declared paths happened.
